**GOTCHA: phase-order Rule A fails (not warns) if an openspec change dir with impl code lacks ANY of proposal/spec/design/tasks**

What: The `phase-order` DETECTION gate (brain/scripts/vcs/phase-order-check.mjs) FAILS (level 'fail', not warn) via Rule A when a PR carries implementation code AND touches an openspec/changes/<dir> that is missing ANY of the four SDD artifacts: proposal.md, spec.md, design.md, tasks.md. `complete = hasProposal && hasSpec && hasDesign && hasTasks`. `hasSpec` folds both conventions: a root `spec.md` OR any `specs/*/spec.md`.

Why it bit us (#219/#220): I shipped issue-219-migrate-v1 with proposal+design+tasks+checkpoint but NO spec.md → phase-order failed on the first push ("implementation without spec.md/design.md"). Fixed by adding spec.md; reproduced locally to `level: pass` before re-pushing.

How to apply: EVERY new openspec change dir that ships impl code needs all four (proposal, spec, design, tasks) — checkpoint-report.md is extra, not counted. Note: brain:repo:check S-1 only enforces proposal.md; phase-order Rule A additionally enforces spec+design+tasks. Local repro: `runPhaseOrderCheck({ baseSha, headSha })` (the CLI wrapper degrades to 'warn' when BASE_SHA/HEAD_SHA are unset, so it silently skips locally unless you pass the SHAs). BASELINE_EXEMPT_DIRS grandfathers only pre-v3 legacy dirs (installer-versionado, vcs-adapter, cli-i18n) — new dirs are never exempt.

phase-order is DETECTION (not one of the 5 REQUIRED), so it doesn't block merge under rung-1 — but a red DETECTION that isn't the expected actor-check is a real signal, never ignore it.
